newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: At least 50 die in runaway train crash in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: At least 50 die in runaway train crash in Pakistan.

text.p: A runaway train crashed in Pakistan's central Punjab province on Monday, killing at least 50 people and injuring up to 100, police and doctors said.
"We have recovered 35 to 40 dead bodies. Ten to 15 bodies are still trapped and it is not easy to take them out," Khanewal town police superintendent Mushtaq Warraich told Reuters.
A doctor at Khanewal's Civil Hospital said 35 bodies had been received there and at least 15 more were en route.
He said 78 injured people were being treated, of whom 22 were in serious condition and would be transferred to the nearby city of Multan, 45 km (28 miles) west of Khanewal.
A spokesman for the private Edhi Trust ambulance service said more than 100 people had been injured on the Zulfikar Express, adding that the death toll could reach 60.
Officials of state-owned Pakistan Railways said the Karachi-bound passenger train had failed to stop at a junction, apparently because of brake failure.
Controllers diverted it on to a dead-end track to prevent a head-on collision with the Lahore-Karachi Shaheen Express train coming the other way on the single main track.
The diverted train then hit the buffers at the end of the spur line near the village of Mirshah, about five km (three miles) from Khanewal, derailing the engine and five coaches.
The engine ploughed through the buffers into a sand barrier at about 4.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Sunday). Two of the coaches were completely crushed, witnesses said.
"Some of the bodies are unrecognisable," Warraich said.
He said rescuers had tried to use blow-torches to free victims from the wreckage but were unable to do so because the carriages were made of inflammable material.
"We have called for manual cutters because gas cutters cannot be used," he said, adding that army technical experts had been called in to help.
One survivor, Muhammad Ashiq, was distraught, wailing and hitting his head with both hands. Seven members of his family died in the crash. They had been on their way to a wedding.
Women from nearby villages gathered at the scene of the carnage, wailing and beating their chests in mourning.

Khanewal residents thronged the hospital to donate blood after appeals broadcast over mosque loudspeakers. Private cars helped ambulances to ferry casualties to the hospital, about 12 km (eight miles) from the scene of the accident.
On January 21, an express train hit a school van at a level crossing at Gujarhan, 60 km (37 miles) south of Islamabad, killing nine people, including six children and two teachers.
